reason: Inner-ear inflammation defines the otologic axis. This etiologically mixed umbrella does not establish infection or immune mediation across its forms.

Red-cell aplasia defines haematologic disease. Ventricular septal defect, cleft palate and structural ear abnormalities with hearing loss each occur in 2/4 reported patients, supporting the three involved axes.
Duane ocular motility abnormalities and radial-ray malformations define the syndrome. Hearing involvement is not established as defining or present in at least 30% of this deletion subtype.
Dwarfism with advanced bone age supports musculoskeletal disease. The sparse record establishes no additional axis; low confidence is appropriate.

The metabolic defect and hemolytic anemia support both primary axes; neurologic impairment occurs in roughly half of systemic cases. A phagocyte-related ancestor alone does not establish common immunodeficiency.

Neurologic and dermatologic disease define NF1. Cardiovascular involvement is not inherited automatically from the RASopathy parent; non-damaging Lisch nodules and minority complications do not warrant additional axes.

Remove ocular: uveitis is an uncommon complication; its supplied frequency tag is clinically unreliable. Retain dermatologic for common necrotic inoculation eschars, rather than transient rash or rare gangrene.

corrected.basis: Orientia infection; necrotic inoculation eschars occur in roughly 40-80%, varying geographically. Uveitis and gangrene are uncommon despite supplied frequency tags; transient rash excluded.

reason: Photosensitive ichthyosis and hair abnormalities define dermatologic disease. Tooth agenesis in 1/2 reported patients supports gastrointestinal involvement; this subtype record does not establish neurologic involvement.
Remove gastrointestinal: feeding aversion, vomiting and reflux do not establish direct intrinsic gastrointestinal damage. Retain ocular for common functional impairment from strabismus.

corrected.basis: Glycosylation defect with universal neurodevelopmental impairment; strabismus occurs in 80-99%. Feeding difficulty, vomiting and reflux do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal injury.

reason: Cerebral vascular amyloid deposition and progressive dementia define cardiovascular and neurologic disease. Hereditary amyloid deposition alone does not establish a separate metabolic or endocrine disorder.
